_readme: Where each Legend stands in the new-build pass (owner 2026-09-05: 'I'll
want this same for all remaining legends. Not in the 9.'). Hand-kept,
because the last stage is his ear and nothing can derive that.
stage:  not started | researched | built | auditioned | confirmed
confirmed means HE HAS HEARD IT AND SAID YES. Nothing else
verdict: his actual words, so the next session doesn't re-litigate it.

Doc Day.verdict: I like b from the new audition. The kick sounds good.
Doc Day.notes: First one. Four research changes (dry snare, working sub under the kick via allow_peak_db, transient shaping, ratio 4.0 bus compression) + own_soundbank + kit tags rewritten to words that match real filenames + snare_locked_24. Took three audition batches to get one he could judge; the first two rendered the config skeleton instead of calling compose().

Razor.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. Nine changes, all in his block only: allow_dirt (his SP-1200 dust 0.6, vinyl -38, wow and 1.35 drive had NEVER played once - clean_renders stripped all of it), wow 0.2->0.5, mix_sat 0->1.5 and kick_dist 0->3.0 ('console into the red'), his own mix_eq with the air CUT to -1.5 dB at 8 kHz (SP-1200 Nyquist ~13 kHz - the era could not make air), space gated->room, jitter 6->8 on kick and snare, kit tags + kick_flavors rewritten to words that match real filenames, own_soundbank on, stamp LANE dropped (owner call - clang/gong/sword matched 1 fx file in 356). glue deliberately LEFT at 1.8, the opposite of Doc Day, because his sources say 'forget about compression, its huge eq work'. Measured new vs old: air -10.3 dB, sub +0.7 dB, attack -1.2 dB. The `roomy` kick tag was in the first render and pulled - it matched Cloud_Roomy_Kick n Hat, a compound one-shot with a hat baked in. Caught by reading the printed sample list.
Razor.verdict: Approved 2026-09-06 from a checklist — he ticked 'keep' for all four new builds. Not his own words; a click, not a sentence.

Mustang.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. He was already CLEAN and his line says 'clean digital', so unlike Razor there was no grime to switch on - the July rule agrees with him. Changes: allow_dirt 'low' + kick_dist 9.0 (808 distorted, mix untouched - owner's call, amount measured over a 4/6/9/12/16 sweep because 4.0 was inaudible); kick jitter 1->3 ms on the KICK LANE ONLY (owner's call, the one place his sources and his own description disagree); the and-of-two kick weight 4->8, which his listen line names and his grammar did not deliver; kit tags fixed and own_soundbank on. HEADLINE: his 'Hey!' chant - the thing Billboard names as his single identifying feature - was pointed at the FX bucket, zero matches in 356 files, while the vox bucket literally contains 'Cymatics - Hey Vox'. Role fx->vox; he is now locked to WUH.wav. Two engine faults fixed on the way: lock_stamps ignored own_soundbank, and the render script crashed on any legend with a clap instead of a snare.
Mustang.verdict: Approved 2026-09-06 from a checklist — he ticked 'keep' for all four new builds. Not his own words; a click, not a sentence.

Farrow.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. This one was not a tuning pass: Farrow was a DUPLICATE of Glass Cat, one of the nine — same 98 bpm, same five lanes, same kit tags word for word, same 18 ms clap flam, both 'built' on The Neptunes / Pharrell. Owner: 'I have a version of him in the 9 I want to keep. I want this build to be a different era than that', and 'Nerd'. So Glass Cat keeps the Neptunes minimal era and Farrow is now N.E.R.D. — which is documented, not invented: they withdrew In Search Of... in 2002 and reissued it re-recorded with a live band, and Pharrell's stated reason was that N.E.R.D. 'was to be an entirely different venture ... the band's music should also sound different'. Changes: clap lane DROPPED (his call, 'give it to Glass Cat alone' — the flam is the Neptunes trait and the loudest reason they sounded alike); HAT lane added, closed/tite/ride, because a rock kit has a hi-hat and the snap-instead-of-hats is Glass Cat's; snap demoted from timekeeper to colour; kick/snare/hat jitter to 3 ms (Coleman: Pharrell plays a kit and they loop 16 bars, 'that's where a lot of the feel comes from'; Hugo 2003: 'Pharrell's playing drums'); the 10% 808 kick branch dropped as the OTHER era's drum machine; kit tags fixed and own_soundbank on; chord_source bell->GUITAR (112 real samples, unused by any legend, and 'live drums and guitars' is quoted). Dirt asked and answered: stay completely clean. HEADLINE FAULT: his producer tag was 'Cymatics - LIFE - Rain and Windchimes 4.wav', a field recording of rain on every beat he ever made, because the open bank wiped his tags; now Drip 2.wav. Two script faults fell out: make_legend_newbuild forced BOTH versions to use the new kit, so a structure-only build rendered byte-identical files (its own 'nothing moved' guard caught it) and then crashed on the lane mismatch — fixed with a --structure mode. LEFT INCONSISTENT ON PURPOSE: the rest of his signature harmony block is still written for the classic-minimal era, and Glass Cat still carries the same dead tags (he is one of the nine, out of scope, owner said keep him).
Farrow.verdict: Approved 2026-09-06 from a checklist — he ticked 'keep' for all four new builds. Not his own words; a click, not a sentence.

Kane East.notes:
He was a DUPLICATE, not out of tune. Sunday Chop in the nine is also built='Kanye West' and the two listen lines were nearly the same sentence — same 57% swing, same driving pushed kicks, same BIG clap with the snare tucked underneath, same tambourine offbeats. Second legend/crew duplicate found the same day (Farrow was a copy of Glass Cat); the legends and the nine are audited separately, which is how both survived. Owner asked directly, then chose the era: Yeezus, over 808s & Heartbreak and Dark Fantasy. Sunday Chop keeps chipmunk soul and was NOT touched.
Rebuilt as the industrial era: bpm 90->130, swing 57->50, jitter 2->0 on kick/clap/snare, the BIG-clap-over-tucked-snare inverted to a stacked 0.8/0.8, tambourine+shaker perc replaced by 84 real toms at 0.55, gated reverb -> dry, allow_dirt True with kick_dist 6.0 and mix_sat 3.0, and the 30% 808 kick_flavors branch dropped. dust 0.35 -> 0.0 and vinyl -44 -> -80: his old line promised a vinyl bed that had never once played, and the honest fix was to stop promising it, not to finally switch a soul-era bed on under an industrial record. Melodic side moved from strings/choir/gospel to synth/pluck/chip and static minor vamps; library tags from soul/motown to electro/house/punk/drill/minimal/techno.
Dead tags found and fixed before own_soundbank went on, in that order: kick 'warm' 0 files, clap 'big' 0, stamp 'vocal' 0 and 'soul' 0, and 'boom' on the kick matched 3 files of which 2 were 808s.
FOURTH WRONG PRODUCER TAG IN FOUR LEGENDS: his locked stamp was 'Cymatics - LIFE - River - Light 4.wav', a field recording of a river, riding every beat he had ever made. Cleared and re-picked to 'wierd ass siren.wav' — Slant Magazine's description of the record names 'slowly morphing drones and sirens' outright. The stamp tags were first written siren/alarm/riser/white-noise (20 files), the lock landed on a white-noise sweep, and they were narrowed to siren/alarm (7) because a riser is not a producer tag.
SCRIPT FIX, and the most reusable thing here: tools/make_legend_newbuild.py now prints the locked stamp at the head of its sample list. build_kit puts it in kit['stamp'] but never in `sources`, so the one sample heard on every single beat was the one sample the 'read the list before you ship it' step could not show. That blind spot is exactly how four wrong producer tags in a row got past it.
Structure build, so a and b share neither a beat nor a tempo (90 vs 130) and the dB numbers compare two different beats: sub -9.37 dB, air +9.20 dB, attack +1.23 dB. The sub drop is intended and documented (short hard kicks, no 808) but it is the biggest single number in the build and it is the thing to listen for.
NOT heard. Only his ear closes it.
Kane East.verdict: Approved 2026-09-06 from a checklist — he ticked 'keep' for all four new builds. Not his own words; a click, not a sentence.

J Dillo.notes:
Rendered and measured, NOT heard. THIRD legend/crew duplicate: he was a copy of Otto Grit in the nine (both built='J Dilla', 88 bpm, same 'drunk pull / snare rushes early / kick leans back late / hats dead straight' line, same snare tags vinyl+dusty+lofi, same hat tags closed+vintage, same gated snare, same drive 1.35, same stamp on bars 4 and 8). Owner picked era 'c': Otto Grit untouched, J Dillo becomes DONUTS 2005-06.
Sourced changes: mix_eq with the air cut (-4 dB at 7 kHz, +2 dB at 110) from the Vox/Earworm line that his 'signature low-end texture' came from 'cutting all high-end frequencies of the sample'; the 45%-808 kick branch DROPPED because on Donuts he chopped kicks and snares out of the records themselves (same call as Kane East); bar_lengths [2,4]->[2] from Red Bull's 'more microchops than 4 bar loops'; bpm 88->84 and loop tempo window 70-95 -> 62-88 from Charnas (Donuts was PRO TOOLS on a laptop, not the MPC/SP-303 myth, and he 'halved the tempo and stretched the loop out ... keeping the pitch constant'); kick_dist 2.0 / mix_sat 1.0 from 'Mash distorts the first piano note of its loop'. Magnitudes are mine and the note says so.
Live faults, not tuning: allow_dirt was absent so dust 0.5 / vinyl -42 / wow 0.15 / drive 1.35 had NEVER PLAYED (Razor's fault again); own_soundbank off so every taste tag was dead code; and the tags were broken - kick 'dust' 0 files of 525, snare 'vinyl' 0 and 'dusty' 0 of 571, kick 'boom' 3 of which 2 were 808s.
ABSOLUTE: 'hats dead straight' is now hats_dead_straight, a choke point in crew.render_crew_beat that zeroes hat offset/jitter/swing and refuses. Its test found a real fault immediately: his hat lane carried 2 ms of jitter against his own word.
STAMP CLEAN for the first time in five legends - Cymatics - LIFE - Vinyl Crackle 29, right for the era, left alone.
HOUSE-WIDE FAULT FOUND HERE: 22 full drum LOOPS from Focusrite_Drum_Pack's BPM folders were sitting in the one-shot hat/crash/perc buckets (Full_Closed_Hats_120 etc, every one measured at exactly 1-2 bars at its stated tempo). The first render of this audition picked Full_Closed_Hats_120 as a hat at 84 bpm, which is how it surfaced. All 22 banned; affected all 23 identities, not just him.
Measured new vs old over 2 beats: air -10.40 dB, sub +3.21 dB, attack +0.58 dB. The air cut is the headline and the thing to judge.
NOT heard. Only his ear closes it.
J Dillo.verdict: Confirmed 2026-09-19 — he listened and said yes.

Just Flame.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. Just Blaze is NOT in the nine (step 1b clean, no era question). Changes, all in his block: space gated->room, which is the one thing his own words actually name -- UAD 2024, he runs the snare through an SPL Transient Designer 'letting me use the NATURAL REVERB, rather than having to use a reverb plug-in', so a gated plug-in was exactly wrong and 'dry' would have been wrong the other way; kit tags rewritten to live filenames then own_soundbank on, in that order (snare big=0 crack=0, clap big=0, stamp swell=0 were all dead, and the find was `stomp` = 29 files under a line that says 'pounding driving kicks'); kick_flavors 808 branch 0.3->0.15 with live tags, description-led not sourced. NO INVARIANT: his listen line has no absolute word in it, so there is nothing to choke -- said out loud rather than inventing one. Sources confirm rather than move sidechain 0.2 and the untouched compression knobs ('over compression... can suck the life, soul and dynamics right out') -- the opposite of Doc Day, do not copy his glue 4.0 here. Rendered with --structure, because holding the kit constant made a kit-only build render two identical files and the guard caught it. Proof in the printed list: OLD picked 'sn2 rim dry.aif' (a sidestick) for the snare and a ride cymbal for the hat; NEW picked Terror Heavy Snare / sn 4 hard and two closed hihats. The 808 branch was then DROPPED and the batch re-rendered: measured over 300 composed beats a declared 15% was delivering a real 38%, because the streak-breaker zeroes a flavor after two repeats and with only two flavors that forces the other to certainty. He is one flavor now, like Farrow, Kane East and J Dillo. STAMPS: this is the first legend rendered after the 2026-09-06 unlock, and his stamp is the crash his line asks for, different on every beat.
Just Flame.verdict: Confirmed 2026-09-19 — he listened and said yes.

Swish Beatz.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. Swizz Beatz is NOT in the nine (step 1b clean). THE INVARIANT: his line ends 'zero subtlety and proud of it', so `zero_subtlety` REFUSES the sparse and displaced backbeat modes on his clap and snare -- 35% of his roll, gone. His HATS are deliberately excluded because the same line asks for 'sparse shouting hats'; widening that test to the hat lane would destroy the character it protects. Choke point is one branch in pattern_gen.compose(), proved red by removing the flag. Tags rewritten then own_soundbank on: kick knock=0 punch=1 -> hard/stomp/dry (stomp=29, and his line's first image is 'big simple kick stomps'), clap big=0 -> clap, stamp horn=0 shout=0 vocal=0 -> siren+stab. THE LIBRARY HAS NO HORN SAMPLES AT ALL (horn=0, brass=0 in all 356 fx) -- his horns come from chord_source, which the Complex 2011 interview independently vindicates ('those types of horns'; 'we would follow the beat... with the melodies'). space/sidechain/drive LEFT and flagged: the sources are about writing and gear and say nothing about reverb or compression. Two corrections mid-build, both caught by reading the printed sample list: `dry` on the snare handed back a sidestick and a rim on both beats (Farrow's note had already warned about it), and the 808 branch was dropped outright after measuring 38% against a declared 15%.
Swish Beatz.verdict: Confirmed 2026-09-19 — he listened and said yes.

Timberline.notes: Was a straight DUPLICATE of Chrome Dial (one of the nine) — same producer, same 100 bpm, same kit tags word for word. Owner 2026-09-07: 'Do whichever era we don't already have built as one of the nine.' Chrome Dial's line names his ASR-10, so he keeps 1996-2002; Timberline moved to the 2006-08 club-pop era (FutureSex/LoveSounds, Loose, Shock Value). 118 bpm, hat lane added, four-on-floor-leaning kick, clap to the backbeat, chord_source wood->synth, arp chord_rhythm + chord_grammar stabs, tags rewritten (kick was matching 4 files of 488), own_soundbank on, stamp block/tabla/cowbell -> tamb. 808 kick branch dropped: measured -5.5 dB sub, +5.2 dB air.
Timberline.verdict: Confirmed 2026-09-19 — he listened and said yes.

DJ Light Green.notes: NEW, the thirteenth — not a rebuild. Owner asked for DJ Green Lantern, picked the roster name himself (DJ Light Green), picked the era (2013+ EDM/trap crossover, not the 2002-06 Invasion mixtapes) and said add as #13, replace nobody. Built from his own words (Vibe 2014): 'marching band trap music with feel good elements... along with some trance in the chord sections with some big percussion elements in there to off-set it.' 140 bpm halftime, long driven 808, buzz/flam/roll snare, 32nd and triplet hat rolls, toms+stomps+cowbell perc, bright major/lydian arps, vocal chops via extras. THE 50% RULE (owner, this session, THIS LEGEND ONLY): snare-on-3 fires on a coin flip and the other half rolls the full grammar menu — measured 20/20 over 40 composes. Doc Day stays locked. Three faults caught before delivery: tags matched almost nothing (kick 3 files of 488, stamp 1 of 353); the stamp lane has been globally OFF since 2026-08-01 so his vocal chops moved to extras; and 'dry' was pulling sidesticks into the snare lane. KNOWN GAP: the engine's kick-variety check still flags his bank as clustered (mean 3.7-4.3 vs floor 4.5) after two passes — sparse halftime trap lines are inherently few moves apart. Shipped rather than fought. ALSO: his 'trance' chords come out as chiptune arps because the melodic index holds 7 pitched samples, all bell — no synth, pluck or chip material exists to sample.
DJ Light Green.verdict: Confirmed 2026-09-19 — he listened and said yes.

Hitt Kid.verdict: I listened to hitt kid yes he's all set.
Hitt Kid.notes:
Rendered and measured, NOT heard. Hit-Boy is not in the nine, so step 1b was clean -- no duplicate, no era to pick. (DJ Premium IS the fourth duplicate: Cutz is also built='DJ Premier'. Found this session, left for its own.)
ERA: asked and answered the OTHER way for once. His drums read club-trap and his chord block reads King's Disease, which looks like a fault. Owner: KEEP THE SPLIT -- his listen line opens 'the modern hybrid', so the two eras are the identity. The July chord research was left untouched.
SOURCE: Sound On Sound 'Inside Track: Hit-Boy' (Paul Tingen, July 2024). What it moved: NOTHING in the numbers, and that is the finding. Clean stays clean (his mixer is there for 'the clarity at the same time'; he checks 808s loud so they don't 'tear through the speakers') -- NO allow_dirt, the opposite call to Razor and J Dillo. Timing stays programmed ('I'm primarily a programmer', FL since ~2002). The two kick flavors stay two, and he says it both ways: 'With 808s, I switch it up ... almost not an 808, more like a Moog sound', and on a stripped beat 'the bass was a one-shot acoustic bass ... THERE'S NO 808.' Confirming rather than changing is the whole result here; no change was invented to look busy.
WHAT CHANGED: the tags, which were nearly all dead, then own_soundbank on, in that order. kick punch/hard/knock -> hard/dry (punch=1 of 488, knock=1); snare crack/clean/trap -> hard/trap (crack=0 of 680); hat trap/closed/tight -> closed/tite (trap=1, tight=1 -- this library spells it `tite`, Mustang's trap again, spelled BY HAND because flavor_match is forward-only and must not go on the twelve existing legends); stamp riser dropped (Kane East: a riser is not a producer tag). Snare is hard/trap and deliberately NOT hard/dry -- Razor's note records `dry` handing back sidesticks.
THE 808 BRANCH: his wants were deep/punch, which match 0 and 1 of the 430 real 808s now reachable via the 2026-09-19 flavor_role fix -- the bass pool's vocabulary is PACK NAMES (cymatics 45, oracle 34, playoffs 30). Left alone they would have funnelled every 808 beat onto one file the moment own_soundbank went on. EMPTIED, exactly as Mustang's were.
NO INVARIANT, said out loud rather than invented: his line has no absolute word in it, and 'halftime and backbeat both in the bag' is the opposite of a lock.
TWO ENGINE FAULTS FOUND ON THE WAY, both older than this pass, both owner-approved roster-wide for the 13 legends (the nine untouched):
  1. The kick-flavor streak-breaker zeroed a flavor after two repeats. With the TWO flavors every legend carries that forces the other to certainty, so declared splits never played: Just Flame's 15% delivered 38% (the number already in his own build note), DJ Light Green's 80% delivered 60%. FOUR legends had their 808 branch DELETED to work around this rather than fixed. Legends exempt now; damping instead of exempting was simulated and rejected (15% only recovered to 28%).
  2. own_soundbank was DEAD on 30% of beats. _pick_path wipes wants/must when open_bank is True BEFORE own_bank is read, so the 2026-09-14 'every DJ picks freely 30% of the time' rule silently beat the 2026-09-05 'rebuilt legends use their own tags' rule for 5 days, on all ten own_soundbank legends. Surfaced because the first render of THIS audition put `hat open.aif` on a man whose tags say closed/tite -- the exact sound own_soundbank exists to prevent. Owner kept both rules and split them by roster: legends 15%, the nine stay 30%.
STAMP CLEAN: Cymatics Impact on both new beats, against Risers on both old ones -- the riser drop is audible and the stamp was right first time, no cached lock.
GAP NAMED IN THE READ ME: both new beats rolled the 808 branch (45% declared, so ordinary luck), so the pair shows his 808 half and NOT his hard-kick half. The two 808s are different files, which is itself the first audible proof of the morning's flavor_role fix.
Structure build, so a and b share neither beat nor form; sub +1.94 dB, air -3.85 dB, attack -0.26 dB compare two different beats and are rough.
ALSO SPOTTED, his library not the engine, nothing touched: 7 open-hat files sit in Hats/Closed (OH _ HEAZY, OH * Blue, [PBS] D Rich Open, offset oh ...). The sorted-folder rule makes them legitimately match `closed`, so they will keep arriving on any DJ asking for closed hats until he refiles them.
NOT heard. Only his ear closes it.

Well Damn.notes:
NEW, the fourteenth — not a rebuild. Owner asked for FnZ (Finatik N Zac) after a research pass, picked the roster name himself (Well Damn, from their producer tag "FNZ, well damn!") and the era (Denzel Curry / ZUU-era Miami bass, not the Drake/Future sample-flip side — on that side another producer usually adds the drums, so there is no FnZ drum identity there to build). Added as #14, replacing nobody. Full sourcing (6 sources) is in legends_config.json["Well Damn"]["signature"]["_note"].
bpm 165 with a halftime clap, sourced from real tempos on FnZ-drummed Denzel tracks (Knotty Head 158, Ricky 169, Shake 88 182, P.A.T. 160, Birdz 156-doubled); kick/clap/hat/perc tags borrowed from the Miami Bass GENRE build done the same session (already tag-audited against real filenames, and legitimate here because Highsnobiety names 2 Live Crew as ZUU's direct inspiration); kick_dist/mix_sat/drive pushed to the roster's most distorted to match "steroidal 808s"/"brash" — flagged as unsourced magnitudes. Added to legends_config.json AND tools/legends.py (LEGENDS_DEFAULT, LEGEND_KICK_BANK, LEGEND_TITLES) so a config regen would not lose him. Roster-count and own_soundbank-set assertions in tests/test_crew.py updated (13->14, set +Well Damn); added to NO_STAMP_LANE alongside Razor/DJ Light Green (kit has a stamp entry, no stamp lane — STAMP_LANE has been False for everyone since 2026-08-01).
BUILT FROM THE CLOUD SANDBOX, NOT HIS MACHINE: this Linux sandbox cannot reach the TBOTC 3 drive or run the real macOS venv (pedalboard is a macOS-only wheel). So the tag audit against real live filenames, the MIDI validity gate, and an actual rendered/heard audition ALL still need to happen on his machine — none of that happened this session. What DID run here: the module imports cleanly, load_legends()/normalize_preset() accept the new entry without error, and tests/test_crew.py -q gives the same 7-failed/33-passed split as the documented pedalboard/external-drive baseline — no NEW failure from this change. NOT heard. Only his ear closes it, and the tag audit needs to happen first.
Well Damn.verdict: (none yet — needs --tags audit and a rendered audition on his machine)
